shortDescription: A surge in wind power generation in Germany pushed the country's day-ahead power contract price down on Thursday.($1 = 0.8612 euros)

children: A surge in wind power generation in Germany pushed the country's day-ahead power contract price down on Thursday.
The German baseload spot electricity contract (TRDEBD1) was down 23% to €96.50 ($112.10) per megawatt hour at 0723 GMT, its lowest since July 24, according to LSEG data.
Wind power in Germany is expected to rise by 10.7 gigawatts to 38.6 GW, while solar power generation is expected to rise by 1.5 GW. Consumption is expected to edge down by 0.5 GW to 51.9 GW.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was similarly down 23% to €115/MWh, its lowest since August 21.
Consumption in France is expected to edge down by 0.7 GW to 44.3 GW, while wind power and solar power are expected to edge up by 0.8 GW and 0.5 GW respectively.
Meteo France warned of temperatures as high as 37 degrees Celsius in southern metropolitan France on Friday and reaching beyond 35 degrees Celsius through the weekend.
French nuclear availability remained stable, at 78% of total availability.
On the forward side, the German 2027 contract (TRDEBYc1) was marginally down by 1% to €122.25/MWh, after hitting its highest level since October 2023 on Wednesday.
"We are now in somewhat of a panic mode on a market, where the 2027 future has increased by around 20% the last month," analysts at Mind Energy wrote.

The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was not traded, according to LSEG data. It hit its highest level since December 2024 on Wednesday, as rising gas prices after renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities added to concerns over winter supply.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
edged down 0.2% to €83.92 a metric ton.
